seo.title: HX Antarctic Circle Expedition: 16 Days on MS Roald Amundsen
seo.description: HX's 16-day Antarctic Circle Expedition from Buenos Aires: the Drake Passage by sea, then nine days on the Peninsula with an attempt south of the Antarctic Circle to Marguerite Bay. The voyage James sailed in 2020.

tagline: South of 66 degrees, by sea: the voyage James sailed in 2020.
answer: The Antarctic Circle Expedition is HX's 16-day voyage from Buenos Aires. After a night in the city and a flight to Ushuaia, MS Roald Amundsen or MS Fridtjof Nansen crosses the Drake Passage and spends Days 5 to 13 on the Antarctic Peninsula, attempting a route through the sea ice and below the Antarctic Circle to Marguerite Bay. Fares from US$12,814 per person, as HX publishes them, with flights between Buenos Aires and Ushuaia, drinks and gratuities included.
overview: HX calls it an attempt, and means it: in the milder summer the sea ice can open a way south of the Antarctic Circle to Marguerite Bay, with islands and remote historical stations along the way. If ice or weather close the route, the captain adapts the voyage.

Days on the Peninsula bring landings by small expedition boat, ice cruising among the bergs and lectures in the onboard Science Center. Kayaking and a night camping on the snow can be added, priced separately and bookable on board.
James sailed this voyage aboard MS Roald Amundsen in February and March 2020, calling at Ukraine's Vernadsky research station as the world shut down behind the ship.

itinerary.title: The beat of Buenos Aires
itinerary.summary: A night in Buenos Aires before the expedition, with breakfast, in a hotel HX arranges. Arrive a few days early to see more of the city.

itinerary.title: Flight to Ushuaia, then board
itinerary.summary: An early flight south to Ushuaia, Tierra del Fuego, to board the ship. Suite guests spend the afternoon before boarding at Arakur Resort & Spa.

itinerary.title: Across the Drake Passage
itinerary.label: Days 3 to 4
itinerary.summary: Two days at sea with the Expedition Team: lectures in the Science Center on Antarctica's history, science and safety, and the Citizen Science projects you can join.

itinerary.title: The Antarctic Peninsula
itinerary.label: Days 5 to 13
itinerary.summary: Landings by small expedition boat, ice cruising among glaciers and bergs, penguins, seals and whales. The captain chooses the landing sites day by day.

itinerary.title: South of the Antarctic Circle
itinerary.label: Days 5 to 13
itinerary.summary: An attempt through the sea ice, south of the Antarctic Circle to Marguerite Bay, looking for Adélie penguins and visiting remote historical stations along the way, as ice allows.

itinerary.title: Back across the Drake
itinerary.label: Days 14 to 15
itinerary.summary: Two days at sea north to Ushuaia: more time in the Science Center, the spa and the on-deck hot tubs.

itinerary.title: Ushuaia, then Buenos Aires
itinerary.summary: Leave the ship in Ushuaia and fly back to Buenos Aires, or stay on with HX's post programmes.

itineraryNote: HX publishes Days 5 to 13 as one block on the Peninsula and calls the route south of the Antarctic Circle an attempt, depending on ice. The order of the two stops in that block is indicative.

faqs: HX calls the route south of the Antarctic Circle to Marguerite Bay an attempt: it depends on the sea ice. If ice, weather or sea do not allow it, the crew offers an adapted itinerary.
Yes. James sailed HX's Antarctic Circle voyage aboard MS Roald Amundsen in February and March 2020, calling at Ukraine's Vernadsky research station, and was at sea when the world shut down for Covid.
The economy flights between Buenos Aires and Ushuaia are included, with a night in Buenos Aires before the voyage. International flights to Buenos Aires are not.
Meals with drinks including wine, beer and spirits, gratuities, Wi-Fi, an expedition jacket, landings and lectures. Kayaking and camping are extra and bookable on board.
How does it differ from Antarctica21's air-cruises?
HX sails the Drake Passage both ways on a 490-guest ship over 16 days; Antarctica21 flies over the Drake to an 88-guest ship on shorter air-cruises.
